name: Comparative Quantification with more of

1.definition: Compares amounts drawn from a specified set or whole.

examples.form: We should keep [more of these samples].

projection.target: The of-phrase fixes the group counted over. More can quantify a plural count domain or an amount of a non-count substance, depending on the complement.
projection.evidence: See the cited discussion and the constructed illustration.

curious.title: More of a particular set
curious.summary: More of followed by a group or a substance compares amounts taken from that group or substance.
curious.body: In We should keep more of these samples, the phrase after of says which set we're drawing from: these samples. Keeping more of them means a bigger share of that set. The word more can count things in a plural group, as in more of these samples, or measure an amount of a substance, as in more of this soup. Which one it is depends on what follows of.

examples.text: We should keep [more of these samples].
Could I have [more of this soup]?

curious.try: Say more of these cookies and more of this milk. Which one counts items, and which one measures an amount?

teacher.summary: Covers more of plus a domain expression, which compares amounts drawn from a specified set or whole.
teacher.explain: In NP[more + PP[of + domain expression]], the of-phrase fixes the group counted over. More can quantify a plural count domain (more of these samples) or an amount of a non-count substance, depending on the complement. This dictionary describes the pattern as comparing amounts drawn from a specified set or whole, and relates it to the true partitive. It is marked provisional, with medium confidence.
teacher.terms: This dictionary treats this as a specialization of the true partitive.

examples.text: We should keep [more of these samples].
Could I have [more of this soup]?

watch_for: A learner might treat more of these samples and more samples as the same, though the of-phrase fixes a specified set to draw from.
teacher.activity: Show a bowl of items and a jug of juice. Students write one sentence with more of plus a plural count noun phrase and one with more of plus a non-count substance.

child.hook: What is the difference between more cookies and more of these cookies?
child.explain: More of these cookies means more from a set you can point to. The words after of tell which set you mean.

examples.text: We should keep more of these samples.
Could I have more of this soup?

child.play: Point at a pile of things and say what you want more of, starting with more of these or more of this.

cite: Reynolds, Brett, ed. 2026. "Comparative Quantification with more of." English Constructionary. https://brettreynolds.ca/constructionary/linguist/positive-degree-partitive-more-001/ (snapshot 2026-11-19, ef810bb).
